b: Editor’s note: GAMA is one of the sponsors of the BoardGameWire newsletter and an advertiser on the site.

Hobby games trade body GAMA has pledged to rebuild confidence among its members after a fresh wave of resignations saw it lose its president, secretary and two other board members at its annual planning meeting in Baltimore last week.

The departures mean five of the organisation’s elected directors have resigned in less than a month, including three of its four officers – heaping further pressure on an association which has struggled to secure a permanent executive director despite more than a year of searching.

GAMA president Meredith Placko, secretary Tiffany Reid and retailer representative John Stephens all resigned during the board’s planning retreat last week, with creator representative Drew Wehrle stepping down soon after.

Their departures follow the resignation of GAMA vice president Ross Thompson last month, which came alongside the news that interim executive director and COO Melinda Prickett was also leaving the organisation.
Clockwise from top left: Meredith Placko, Tiffany Reid, Drew Wehrle and John Stephens
Placko confirmed her resignation to BoardGameWire on Sunday, just seven months after she was elected president on a platform of improving communication and making GAMA more proactive in its work.

She has since declined to comment on the circumstances surrounding her departure. Buried Giant Studios’ Drew Wehrle confirmed to BoardGameWire that he had submitted his resignation after GAMA’s planning weekend had concluded, but declined to comment further. Stephens told BoardGameWire he was unable to comment “at this time”, while Reid is yet to respond.

GAMA’s board has elected former president Eric Price back into the role following Placko’s departure, while Hammerdog Games’ Danny O’Neill has been elected secretary. Price was previously president from early 2023 until April 2024, when he was succeeded by Nicole Brady.

The association said in an email to members that Stephens was stepping down from the board to focus on his work with Team Retail – the retailer member group within GAMA – but did not give reasons for the other three departures, or address whether any of the resignations were connected.

GAMA said in a statement to members, “We recognize that these changes may be disappointing. Restoring the Board to full strength is a top priority, along with supporting our staff and ensuring successful GAMA Expo and Origins Game Fair events.
“We’re committed to clear communication, rebuilding member confidence, and moving forward to make GAMA even stronger in 2027.”
The latest departures leave GAMA facing its third round of special elections in little more than a year, having only completed the process of replacing Thompson on the board earlier this month.
Cascade Games founder Tim Shields was elected to fill Thompson’s Media & Events seat, bringing more than 30 years of industry experience to the board across retail, publishing and organised play.
Ross Thompson, who resigned from the GAMA board last month
Thompson himself had only joined the board in October last year, winning a special election to replace former secretary Monica Rasso, who had stepped down after five years as a director.

GAMA said Team Retail would nominate one of its members to fill Stephens’ seat, with special elections being held to fill the vacancies in the publisher, wholesaler and creator membership divisions. Self-nominations for those elections are due to open today and run until December 9, with voting scheduled to take place from December 10 to 17.

Red Raccoon Games’ Jamie Mathy remains as treasurer, with former president Nicole Brady, Heather O’Neill, Eartha Johnson, Michael Maggiotto Jr and newly elected director Tim Shields making up the rest of the eight-strong board alongside Price and O’Neill.
The scale of GAMA’s recent leadership upheaval comes amid a period of substantial growth for the organisation, which has significantly expanded its membership, staff and events in recent years.

But the high turnover at both board and executive level raises questions about whether GAMA’s governance structure has kept pace with that growth – from the demands placed on its unpaid directors, to the division of responsibilities between its elected board and professional staff.
Last October GAMA unveiled its first-ever ten-year strategic plan, setting out its ambitions to become the “epicenter” of the global tabletop gaming industry.

But the association has also had a series of difficulties with its communication and relationship with members during that period, including its board being forced to issue an apology for the conduct of some of its directors at this year’s annual general meeting in March.

Several GAMA members had expressed anger at being shouted at and talked over by directors during a heated discussion over proposed changes to the organisation’s bylaws, which had included moves to lower the quorum requirement for membership meetings from 25% to 10%.

The board had argued at the time that GAMA’s rapid growth in recent years had made it increasingly difficult to push through changes to the way the organisation operated, while some members suggested the onus should instead be on GAMA to better communicate with its membership and encourage greater participation.
It subsequently postponed the vote on the proposed amendments, acknowledged shortcomings in its communication with members and apologised to GAMA staff over the incident.

Placko, who was elected president the following month ahead of incumbent Nicole Brady, had identified improving GAMA’s communication as one of her priorities during an extensive interview with BoardGameWire in May.

She said at the time that she wanted to put proactive structures in place to prevent the organisation from “stepping in the mud all the time”, as well as making better use of data in its decision-making and working to turn its ten-year plan into a reality.

Placko had also been particularly vocal in her praise of Prickett and GAMA’s staff following her election, saying, “While the board may have seen a change in leadership, we are a small piece of the GAMA puzzle.
“I want to make sure Melinda, and the staff who are doing the heavy lifting of this organization, get the recognition they deserve.”

Prickett’s departure earlier this month, less than 14 months after she joined GAMA as its first-ever COO, left the organisation facing another unexpected change of executive leadership amid its ongoing difficulties appointing a permanent replacement for John Stacy.
Stacy announced his departure last October after seven years in the role, during which time GAMA substantially expanded both its membership and the size of its annual B2B trade show, GAMA Expo.
Former GAMA executive director John Stacy, who is yet to be permanently replaced after stepping down more than a year ago

GAMA initially said it expected to appoint a permanent replacement for Stacy by spring this year, having brought in leadership consultant Zaria Davis as interim executive director last November. Prickett subsequently took over the role in May.

Placko and Reid told BoardGameWire in late October that GAMA’s board had interviewed a strong candidate for the permanent position and entered negotiations with them, but had been forced to begin the search again after those discussions proved unsuccessful.

Foam Brain Games boss Andrew Zorowitz was brought in as acting executive director earlier this month on a six-month contract, which includes provision for him to remain in the role through next June’s Origins Game Fair if a permanent executive director has not been appointed by then.

GAMA said in its latest update to members that it was narrowing its choice of executive search firm and expected to provide an update at its December board meeting, with the aim of having a permanent executive director in place before next April’s GAMA Expo – about a year later than its original target.

The organisation has also experienced significant turnover elsewhere in its senior staff in recent years, with July’s appointment of Kevin Ronnebaum as senior marketing and communications director making him GAMA’s sixth communications head in as many years.

That turnover has not always been acrimonious – Ronnebaum’s predecessor Eric Francis remained full of praise for GAMA and its staff when speaking to BoardGameWire about his departure earlier this year, saying his decision to leave essentially came down to pay.

Francis’ own predecessor Amy Lowe, however, levelled a series of criticisms at the organisation on her resignation last April, including accusations of “rampant gatekeeping”, “toxic leadership” and disrespecting its members – a characterisation of GAMA’s staff which Stacy disputed at the time.

GAMA said its board had used last week’s meeting in Baltimore to discuss the organisation’s finances, its search for a permanent executive director and preparations for GAMA Expo, and had approved additional expenditure under its 2026 budget for staff technology and other operational needs.

And new president Price has sought to reassure members over the state of the organisation following the latest resignations, which come just over four months ahead of GAMA Expo’s first outing in its new Baltimore home.
He said, “Leadership transitions can be challenging, and we understand that these Board departures may be disappointing to our members.
“Our immediate priorities are restoring the Board to full strength, hiring a permanent Executive Director, and supporting our staff as they prepare for GAMA Expo and Origins Game Fair 2027.

“GAMA is on solid financial footing, and planning for both events is progressing well. We remain firmly committed to our 10-year strategic vision and to strengthening GAMA’s role in supporting and advancing the tabletop game industry.”
